F.I.R. of the present case was lodged against applicant and two others and in the F.I.R., there was allegation of torture and demand of dowry against the husband of the informant but in the F.I.R., it is further mentioned that on 04.07.2021 the marriage of the informant was performed with her nandoi i.e. applicant and thereafter applicant forcibly committed rape with her.
It is further mentioned in the F.I.R. that applicant forcibly committed rape with her for almost a week.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is nandoi of the informant and he has falsely been implicated in the present matter only due to the reason that the dispute of the informant was pending with her husband.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted, although there is allegation that applicant committed rape with informant and her second marriage was also forcibly performed with the applicant by her husband and mother-in-law but entire allegation prima-facie appears to be totally false and no reliance can be placed on such version.
6.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted, although as per allegation, marriage of the informant was performed with the applicant against her wishes on 04.07.2021 and on 11.07.2021,
she has returned to her paternal home but in spite of that, she moved application for lodgement of the F.I.R. on 04.08.2021 and this inordinate delay in moving the application for lodging of the F.I.R.
clearly suggests that belatedly a false story has been cooked up by the informant to falsely implicate the applicant.
7.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that during trial, informant of the case has declared hostile, as she did not support the prosecution case and her statement recorded before the trial court has been annexed alongwith the supplementary affidavit filed in support of the instant bail application.
8. He further submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 21.08.2021 i.e. for more than two years, therefore, he may be released on bail.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
10.
I have heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. Although in the F.I.R. as well as in both the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., there is allegation of rape against the applicant but applicant is nandoi of the informant and matrimonial dispute is pending between the informant and her husband.
12.

Further as per allegation, the marriage of the informant was forcibly performed with her nandoi i.e. applicant by her husband and mother-in-law and thereafter applicant forcibly committed rape with her.
The story narrated by the informant appears to be quite improbable.
13. Further F.I.R. of the present case was lodged quite belatedly after more than a month from the date of alleged rape.
14. Further from the record, it reflects that during trial when informant of the case appeared before the trial court then she did not support the prosecution case and has been declared hostile.

16. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
17. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

18. Let the applicant-Akram, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
19. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

20. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
